title: Revalidation evidence — the value of pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; software-analysis DEC-001 point 7): executed results that confirm or refute an analysis artefact at a commit — a test run against a use case, a trace through a journey. This capability runs nothing: the results arrive from a capability that runs them, or from the project's own filler file. One entry per result, keyed by three parts — the artefact, the commit and the check: its `id` is `<artefact>@<commit>#<check>`. So two fillers' results for one artefact at one commit stand side by side, and only two that claim one check collide. The point is `union`, no default takes part, and its inert policy is `fallback`, because the evidence advises: a revalidation record copies the entries it draws on as support for an artefact's outcome and never in place of one, and only a revalidation or a deferral recorded on the artefact clears friction (COR-050). It reads alone, since two providers of the point are compared by this file alone (COR-053 point 5): its `$defs` carry copies of `analysis.schema.json`'s id, commit, check name and text definitions, their one home, and a test holds each copy equal to its source. The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

evidence.description: The result of one executed check, for one artefact at one commit.

id.description: The entry's key, the three parts it is for: `<artefact>@<commit>#<check>`, exactly the entry's own `artefact`, `commit` and `check`. A schema cannot compare fields, so software-analysis' check holds a revalidation record's copy of an entry to it, and warns on an entry of the point that is not. A record finds the entry by it.

artefact.description: The artefact the run confirms or refutes.

commit.description: The commit the run was made against: the version of the system the result is true of, by its full name.

check.description: The executed check that gave the result: the name its filler gives it, kept from commit to commit (DEC-001 point 7). A filler gives each result it reports for one artefact at one commit a check of its own — one filler never supplies an id twice, and the whole filler is inert if it does. A capability's checks open with the capability's own name, and a project file's with `project`: software-analysis warns on a capability's entry whose check opens with another name and never refuses one, because the project replaces a capability's entry by writing one under that capability's check. A test's name is slugged — `tests/test_run.py::test_sandbox` becomes `pytest-bridge.test-run.test-sandbox` — and kept exactly in `ran`.

result.description: `passed`: the run did what the artefact describes — support for `holds`. `failed`: it did not — a regression with proof attached, or a sign the analysis is stale; the revalidation decides which (DEC-001 points 5 and 7).

ran.description: What was run, so a person can find it and run it again: a test by its name (`tests/test_run.py::test_sandbox`), a trace, a scripted walk through a journey.

steps.description: A set: for a use case, the steps and variants the run went through, by number and letter; for a journey, the use cases it passed through, by id, each once; an actor or a term has none.

where.description: Where the result can be read: a pipeline run, a report file.

by.description: Who or what ran it — a pipeline, a person; on an entry the project writes in place of a capability's, who wrote it.

actor-id.description: An actor's id: `ACT-` and a slug, stable across renames; the key of its entry in the actors' collection file.

term-id.description: A glossary term's id: `TERM-` and a slug, separate from the term's display name, so a rename breaks nothing that cites it; the key of its entry in the glossary.

use-case-id.description: A use case's id: `UC-` and its number within the project, independent of any grouping by area — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000 (`UC-007`), and no leading zero from 1000 on (`UC-1000`), so each number has one spelling and `UC-0007` is never a second id for `UC-007`.

journey-id.description: A journey's id: `JRN-` and its number within the project — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000, and no leading zero from 1000 on, so each number has one spelling.

artefact-id.description: The id of any analysis artefact.

commit.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal name in lower case: 40 digits under SHA-1, 64 under SHA-256. An abbreviated name is refused, so a commit has one spelling and a citation matches an entry exactly.

check-name.description: The name of an executed check: lower-case words of letters, digits and hyphens, joined by dots, the first beginning with a letter (`pytest-bridge.test-run.test-sandbox`). Underscores, slashes, colons and capitals are refused, so a test's name is slugged to fit; the name stands after the `#` of an evidence id.

evidence-id.description: The id of an entry of the evidence point, `pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence` (DEC-001 point 7): the artefact, the commit and the check the result is for, `<artefact>@<commit>#<check>` — an artefact id as above, then a commit's full name, then a check's name. A pattern cannot refer to another, so this one spells the four id shapes, the commit and the check name again, here beside them; a test holds them in step.
